title: Ariana Grande May or May Not Be Struggling. We Can Talk About It Without Trying to Shame Her
description:
“It’s so confusing sometimes to be a girl.”

	Over the past several years, there’s been an ongoing — and, in many cases, much-needed — conversation
body:
“It’s so confusing sometimes to be a girl.”

	Over the past several years, there’s been an ongoing — and, in many cases, much-needed — conversation around pop stars and body image. In 2020, Taylor Swift disclosed to Variety’s Chris Willman that she would sometimes “just stop eating” and had developed an “unhealthy” relationship with food, a pattern she characterized as a Pavlovian response to constant feedback on her size from outside observers. In dialogue with Charli xcx on a remix of 2024’s “Girl, so confusing,” Lorde sang about a “war with [her] body” that entailed starving herself and then gaining the weight back — the latter seeming to cause her as much emotional pain as the former. She further elaborated in her 2025 album “Virgin,” admitting she got “sucked in” by bodily measurements like a “new waist-to-hip” ratio on a song aptly titled “Broken Glass.”
	

	To many fans, these revelations were welcome. Just as Swift distills universal experiences like loss and heartbreak, so too can she put to words what many people feel in a world where bodies are constantly on display. The pressures Lorde faces as an exceptionally visible person are more intense than the average social media user’s inner turmoil over whether and how to edit a selfie, but they’re identical in nature. It’s reassuring to have community in that struggle, and to hear that it’s possible to come out the other side.


	Now, Ariana Grande and the millions of eyes on her have again kicked that conversation into high gear. But this time, there’s one stark and essential difference: Grande hasn’t joined the conversation on her own terms. She’s been conscripted into it.
	

	Concerns about Grande’s noticeably thin appearance had already been percolating since her back-to-back press tours for the blockbuster “Wicked” and its sequel “For Good,” but her new album “Petal,” the much-dissected music video for the title track and her current “Eternal Sunshine” tour have added fuel to the fire. Grande’s representatives announced on Sunday that after the tour, she plans to take “a step back from visibility” amid “endless, ongoing public scrutiny.” To that end, Grande has backed out of an upcoming commitment to star in a West End revival of Stephen Sondheim’s “Sunday in the Park with George.” But the statement made no mention of Grande’s physical or mental state apart from a clause about “finishing the tour…healthily and happily.”

	On Monday, Grande put the news in her own words, while still largely avoiding specifics. “The announcement that was made yesterday was not a reactive or impulsive thing,” the singer said, without naming what she might be seen as reacting to. The “negativity” her reps cited is not keeping her from enjoying this moment of her career, she claimed. But “multiple things can be true at the same time. Yes, boundaries, they need to be set. Human beings can need a break sometimes.” 

	Since the release of “Petal,” social media has been flooded with screenshots showing Grande’s visible ribcage and speculation on her potential use of a prosthetic chest in one sequence of the video. Horrified, some users have shared close-ups of a handwritten list that partly reads, “Couldn’t hurt to lose a few LBs.” It should be noted that, in the video’s narrative, this sentiment isn’t expressed by Grande herself; instead, it’s an observation from a committee of male gatekeepers who pronounce her “not good enough.” But that discrepancy only complicates the matter even further.

	The video, directed by Christian Breslauer, is about Grande rejecting others’ expectations. In it, she plays an anxious aspiring starlet who auditions for a panel of leering Hollywood types at “Fame, Inc.” who ignore her talent, instead finding ways to criticize her appearance no matter how she presents herself. “Should get some work done,” the execs note at one point; “Too much work done,” they write in the next sequence — the one in which fans believe she used a breastplate. Eventually, she snaps and picks up a chainsaw, earning the gratitude of all the women auditioning alongside her. 
	

	There’s certainly a worthy point somewhere in Grande’s allegorical rebellion. Given the response to the video, though, it’s downright jarring to watch the action play out to defiant lyrics like “I don’t need someone to save me” and “This is not a cry for help.” Together, the implication is that discourse about women’s bodies is always out of bounds, no matter the tone or source. But lumping together nitpicking haters and concerned well-wishers isn’t an honest way forward.

	It’s true that the conversation about Grande’s body online has been cruel and unproductive. The most extreme online perspectives unfairly paint Grande as an eager proponent of anorexia — a villain proudly encouraging her massive fandom to join her on a journey of self-deprivation. On the other end of the spectrum, there are hyperdefensive stans who declare that their pop idol is healthier than ever and hurl death threats at anyone who dares to wonder if there’s a problem. Therefore, finding a constructive middle ground between these two poles is the difficult yet worthwhile task before us.

	We are now left at a place where several indisputable and yet conflicting truths ram into each other. One is that Grande is a public figure sharing work with an audience that has every right to respond, form opinions and share their own experiences, including those related to disordered eating. Another is that none of the laypeople sharing their thoughts online are medical professionals with firsthand knowledge of Grande’s diet, exercise, health history or symptoms; armchair diagnoses, even ones based on genuine, logical concern, can be irresponsible.

	Yet another of those truths is that there’s a tangible danger in declaring that we should never comment on other people’s bodies. Grande herself has a responsibility to her fans, many of them impressionable young girls, who may interpret photos of the star slotting comfortably inside a narrow guitar case as an aspirational ideal rather than cause for alarm. It isn’t a cruel instinct or a parasocial delusion to point that out. Organizations dedicated to eating disorder treatment and prevention encourage creatives to employ nuance in depictions of anorexia and similar illnesses. “Avoid using pictures of emaciated individuals” and “stereotypical images” like empty plates and other items meant to symbolize thinness, one such media guide advises. Of course, social media is meant to feel casual — not subject to the same standards and guidelines as music and films released via corporate media entities. Still, Grande and her camp are well aware that a sizable contingent of her followers believe she may have an eating disorder. They don’t have to acknowledge that in public, but must know that snapshots of her on Instagram are being consumed through that lens. 
	

	And finally, there’s the reality that even when a person absolutely needs help, they typically have to want it, too. If the goal is truly to help Grande get well, such extreme external pressure is likely counterproductive.

	The fact of the matter is that none of us — the authors of this column included — understand Grande’s life intimately enough to draw definitive conclusions about her health, as “obvious” as the signs may seem. Yes, her body looks different than it used to. Even drastically so. But there are an unlimited number of reasons a person’s appearance can change. Many of them are terrifying, and few are solved through public comment or intervention.

	For years, people laughed about “Black Panther” star Chadwick Boseman appearing to be tired of crossing his arms across his chest to symbolize “Wakanda Forever.” In the early days of his Marvel fame, he enthusiastically reciprocated the gesture to any fan who offered it to him first. As is the case with the most obsessive observers of Grande’s body, they wanted to feel close to him. With time, though, Boseman began making the motion with a faraway look in his eyes and his arms held weakly in front of his navel. Memes were made and headlines were written about his weariness, with some going as far as to label him ungrateful. But the joke became a lot less funny when his family shocked the world by announcing he had died after privately suffering from colon cancer.

	This isn’t to say that Grande’s struggles can be explained by Boseman’s. The latter case is nonetheless a cautionary tale about the limits of using isolated, curated tidbits of a person’s life to make them the poster child for something bigger. The upper echelons of pop music can indeed be a breeding ground for disordered eating, as Grande’s peers have attested. But if Grande ever does admit to such struggles, it will likely — and probably should — be after the fact, incorporating the hindsight that comes with recovery.

	Until that hypothetical future, shouting from the rooftops that Grande is anorexic and in crisis doesn’t do much to save her or the young people she’s supposedly harming. Shame is rarely, if ever, an effective tool for healing. There is room to gently point out that the images we’re seeing of Grande appear abnormal. At the very least, they resemble tendencies that might be cause for intervention with a real-life loved one. Acknowledging that resemblance is an essential act of empathy — as is offering Grande some benefit of the doubt. As onlookers, the best we can do is hope Grande’s time away gives her space to find what she needs, whatever that may be.
	

	Nearly 20 years after Britney Spears shaved her head, the world has come to understand that they should have spoken about her body and mental health differently. With Grande, and with other stars who will inevitably find themselves in her shoes, we can course-correct. We can choose to be generous, to act in a way we won’t later regret. And we can do that without demanding to hear her secrets.

schema.headline: Ariana Grande May or May Not Be Struggling. We Can Talk About It Without Trying to Shame Her

title: Roger Federer’s Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony Set to be Broadcast on the Tennis Channel (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Tennis Channel announced it will exclusively broadcast the 2026 International Tennis Hall of Fame induction ceremony.

	This year’s event will honor
body:
Tennis Channel announced it will exclusively broadcast the 2026 International Tennis Hall of Fame induction ceremony.

	This year’s event will honor 20-time major champion Roger Federer and journalist and former professional player Mary Carillo. Veteran Tennis Channel analyst Brett Haber will open the celebration, with sports journalist Tom Rinaldi serving as master of ceremonies.

	The ceremony will air live on Tennis Channel and stream on the Tennis Channel app Aug. 29 at 6:30 p.m. ET. The induction will take place at the International Tennis Hall of Fame in Newport, Rhode Island. 
	

	“TC Live” will be on the grounds in Rhode Island for a pre-show beginning at 6 p.m. ET. The pre-show will feature Hall of Famer Martina Navratilova, Prakash Amritraj and Dani Klupenger. 


	Former pro, coach and commentator Brad Gilbert will be on-site to host a special episode of Tennis Channel’s “The Big T” podcast, which is set to air Saturday morning before the festivities.

	Tennis Channel, Tennis Channel 2 and the Tennis Channel app will be showcasing the best of Federer’s on-court moments at matches beginning Aug. 28 and throughout the weekend.

	Federer is the first man to win 20 major singles titles—eight titles at Wimbledon, six at the Australian Open, five at the US Open and one at the French Open (Roland-Garros)—and will be honored for his storied career. 

	Carillo is a former professional tennis player turned broadcasting pioneer known for storytelling and advocacy for the game. She joined Tennis Channel as a commentator in 2011.

schema.headline: Roger Federer’s Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony Set to be Broadcast on the Tennis Channel (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘Mystery Science Theater 3000: The RiffTrax Experiments’ Sets Online Release Schedule
description: “Mystery Science Theater 3000: The RiffTrax Experiments” has officially set release dates for the four new episodes of the beloved cult classic seri
body:
“Mystery Science Theater 3000: The RiffTrax Experiments” has officially set release dates for the four new episodes of the beloved cult classic series. 

	The first episode, which features the movie “Sting of Death,” will debut online on Oct. 9, followed by the “Deathsport” episode on Oct. 23. After that, the mystery third episode will become available on the RiffTrax Best Friends streaming service starting Oct. 30 before becoming available to the general public on Nov. 6. Finally, the “Space Raiders” episode (which will feature the onscreen returns of Trace Beaulieu and Frank Conniff) drops on Nov. 20. All episodes will be released ahead of the 2026 Turkey Day marathon, a longstanding “Mystery Science Theater” fan tradition. 
	

	As previously reported, all episodes will be available via RiffTrax.com. All Kickstarter backers that supported at any of the reward levels that include a download of an episode will receive a free month of Best Friends, which they can redeem starting on Oct. 16. 


	The “Sting of Death” episode will also screen in theaters across the country on Sept. 9, with a special encore matinee Sept. 13. 

	Variety exclusively reported in February that RiffTrax and Shout! Studios teamed to produce four new episodes of “MST3K.” RiffTrax stars and original series alums Michael J. Nelson, Kevin Murphy, and Bill Corbett are all returning both in front of and behind the camera. Mary Jo Pehl is also returning as Pearl Forrester. Filming took place earlier this year in Minneapolis, where the original series was filmed. 

	Nelson, Corbett, and Murphy have been performing under the RiffTrax banner since 2006. In that time, they have riffed over 1,000 short films, major blockbusters, hilarious low-budget fare, TV shows, and more. They also frequently host RiffTrax live screenings where they live riff a movie in front of an audience.

schema.headline: ‘Mystery Science Theater 3000: The RiffTrax Experiments’ Sets Online Release Schedule

title: Christina Applegate Returns Home After Months-Long Hospitalization and ‘All Is Well’
description: Christina Applegate has returned home following a months-long hospitalization amid her ongoing battle with multiple sclerosis. News broke in late Ma
body:
Christina Applegate has returned home following a months-long hospitalization amid her ongoing battle with multiple sclerosis. News broke in late March that the 54-year-old Emmy winner had been hospitalized, with outlets like the Daily Mail and Page Six reporting at the time that those close to Applegate were preparing for the worst. But the actor spoke out on Instagram in April and told fans she was “getting stronger and better every day.”
	

	A source told Variety that “all is well” with Applegate amid the news of the actor’s return home.


	Applegate announced in August 2021 that she had been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis. The specifics of her hospitalization remain unclear, although she has been outspoken over the last few years about the challenges she faces while living with MS. Applegate speaks frankly about her diagnosis and its side effects (from intense bouts of nausea to swollen limbs, vertigo and more) on the podcast she hosts with “Sopranos” star Jamie-Lynn Sigler, who also has MS.  

	“Thank you for the outpouring of love and well wishes,” Applegate wrote on Instagram amid her hospitalization. “Health issues are a constant for me, but I’m a strong chick and I’m getting stronger and better every day. I’m taking a moment to focus on my health, but I’ll be back with more to say soon enough.”

	News of Applegate’s hospitalization broke a few weeks after the publication of her memoir, “You With the Sad Eyes.” She embarked on a press tour for the book with virtual appearances on talk shows such as ABC’s “The View” and more. Applegate, who is best known for the “Anchorman” movie and for starring in Fox sitcom “Married… with Children,” retired from acting while dealing with her MS. The comedic thriller series “Dead to Me” was her final role, with the show’s third season filming amid her diagnosis.

schema.headline: Christina Applegate Returns Home After Months-Long Hospitalization and ‘All Is Well’

title: Eli Roth Got Sick of Studio Notes and Shrinking Residuals, With ‘Ice Cream Man’ He’s Going Into Business for Himself
description: When Eli Roth was making “Borderlands,” a $120 million adaptation of a popular video game, he felt the movie getting farther and farther away from h
body:
When Eli Roth was making “Borderlands,” a $120 million adaptation of a popular video game, he felt the movie getting farther and farther away from his punk rock vision.

	“As things grow bigger, studios just naturally become more risk averse,” Roth says. “My nature as a filmmaker is to do the thing that’s left of center, because that’s what has worked for me.”

	But to earn a PG-13 rating, studio executives pushed for cuts and tweaks, and the finished product was a disaster, bombing with audiences and critics when it opened in 2024.
	

	“You got something that belonged to nobody,” Roth says. “It’s not a kids’ movie, but it’s trying to appeal to everybody. It’s for gamers, but it doesn’t have the violence the gamers want because it can’t be that extreme because it costs too much. You just wind up with a movie that’s neither fish nor fowl.”


	That’s not the case with “Ice Cream Man,” which — love it or hate it — is unabashedly Roth’s vision. The director, who made a name for himself directing gorefests like “Hostel” and “The Green Inferno,” is returning to his ultraviolent roots with the story of children who become homicidal maniacs when they devour frozen treats.

	“I thought, what if it’s like the Pied Piper, and the ice cream truck music triggers a Pavlovian response?” Roth says. “I had this image of the kids killing their parents and teachers and then eating more and more ice cream.”

	And this time Roth won’t be pressured to tone down the carnage. He’s cut out the studio entirely and gone into business for himself. Roth raised the film’s $5.5 million budget mostly through foreign pre-sales and tax credits (it shot in Canada). He will release the picture via The Horror Section, the independent genre company that Roth founded in 2025. The plan is to distribute two to four horror films annually in theaters, keeping budgets low to preserve creative freedom. After “Ice Cream Man” opens on Aug. 7, The Horror Section will release “Stiletto,” a slasher film set in strip clubs, in the fall and go into production on “Don’t Go in That House, Bitch!,” a horror film that will team Roth with Snoop Dogg. All of them will get theatrical releases of roughly 45 days.
	

	For “Ice Cream Man,” Roth expects to spend a few million dollars on marketing. That’s a fraction of what studios typically shell out to promote films. The production will rely primarily on cheaper digital ads and stunts such as having Roth show up at Comic-Con to hand out sweet delights from a blood-spattered ice cream truck. If the movie makes between $6 million and $8 million theatrically, Roth estimates it will be profitable because it will earn roughly the same amount on home entertainment.

	“We have set the film up so that the floor is very high,” says Jon Schnaars, The Horror Section’s CEO. “It really does not need to do a lot domestically for us to be well positioned as a company.”

	More importantly, Roth gets to control the stories he spins in perpetuity, instead of selling a script and its underlying IP to a studio for a one-time fee.

	“Novelists who write stories own the underlying rights, but filmmakers who write a screenplay don’t own the underlying rights, and that always felt like an imbalance to me,” Roth says. “Stephen King owns all of his creations. Why should I create something and then give away ownership?”

	That’s become increasingly important as the economics of moviemaking have shifted in the Netflix era.

	“Decades ago, the studio owning the movie was fine because there was so much money to be made on home video, and we were all doing great,” Roth says. “DVD was explosive, and then you would get residuals when it went to cable TV. But as the streamers came in, all of a sudden, the residuals were gone. When a movie goes on Netflix, you’re not getting any money.”

	“Ice Cream Man” will be released without a rating, sparing it from battles with the ratings board over scenes of preteens vivisecting and decapitating grown-ups. That’s a freedom Roth fought for and frequently lost throughout his career.

	“Part of horror is you’re being distasteful,” Roth says. “And for people in studios, it’s hard to be distasteful because they’re making stuff that they want to be celebrated and socially acceptable. And part of what you’re doing by making a good horror movie is you’re being transgressive and you’re pushing the boundaries.”

schema.headline: Eli Roth Got Sick of Studio Notes and Shrinking Residuals, With ‘Ice Cream Man’ He’s Going Into Business for Himself

title: ‘Colin From Accounts’ Season 3 Trailer: Gordon and Ashley Deal With the Awkward Proposal Gone Wrong (TV News Roundup)
description: After a failed proposal between Gordon (Patrick Brammall) and Ashley (Harriet Dyer), “Colin From Accounts” picks up right where the characters awkwa
body:
After a failed proposal between Gordon (Patrick Brammall) and Ashley (Harriet Dyer), “Colin From Accounts” picks up right where the characters awkwardly left off in the new trailer for Season 3.

	An official synopsis of the final season reads: “Gordon and Ashley are determined to move on from past embarrassments, they can’t seem to shake their collective baggage. And even as life moves relentlessly on, with challenges at work, ongoing family battles and new friendship dramas, something keeps pulling this flawed, funny pair back into each other’s orbits. Do Gordon and Ashley belong together — or is their beloved dog Colin the only thing keeping their futures intertwined?”
	

	New additions to the cast this season include Thomas Cocquerel (“All Her Fault”), Nikki Shiels (“The Last Anniversary”) and Mark Trevorrow (“The Bob Downe Show, Kath & Kimderella”). Returnees include Emma Harvie, Genevieve Hegney, Michael Logo, Helen Thomson, Darren Gilshenan, Virginia Gay, Annie Maynard, Celeste Barber, Justin Rosniak and Tai Hara.


	In a joint statement, show creators and lead stars Brammall and Dyer said: “Creatively it feels like the right time to say goodbye to ‘Colin From Accounts’ after three seasons. We love everything about making this show. From writing all 24 episodes and producing with our amazing partners at Easy Tiger, to acting on set with our brilliant cast and spunky crew, to sitting in the edit with our wonderful post team where we are currently wrapping things up. We’re going to miss making this show terribly, but we hope you love season three as much as we do. Thank you for watching, it means the world.”
	

	Season 3 will premiere Thursday, Sept. 10 on Paramount+ with all eight episodes. The series is produced by Easy Tiger Productions and CBS Studios.

	Watch the trailer below.


	
		RENEWALS	

	“The Artful Dodger” has been renewed for Season 3 at Disney+.

	The Australian Hulu original stars Thomas Brodie-Sangster (“The Queen’s Gambit”), David Thewlis (“Avatar: Fire and Ash”) and Maia Mitchell (“Never Goin’ Back”), who reprise their roles as Dr. Jack Dawkins, Norbet Fagin and Lady Belle Fox. The series adapts the lead character from Charles Dickens’ “Oliver Twist” novels as the pickpocket faces ripple effects from his life of crime in London.

	“Audiences will journey even further into the world of ‘The Artful Dodger’ with the return of our fan-favourite series and can expect even more twists and turns in this third and final instalment,” says Kylie Watson-Wheeler, SVP and managing director of The Walt Disney Company Australia and New Zealand. “The renewal is a testament to the quality of this show, and everyone involved in making it. We’re thrilled to be bringing Australia’s premium storytelling and high-calibre talent and creatives to audiences around the world on Disney+ and Hulu.”

	Filming will take place in Australia in the coming months. The first two seasons are streaming on Disney+ globally and on Hulu in the U.S.

schema.headline: ‘Colin From Accounts’ Season 3 Trailer: Gordon and Ashley Deal With the Awkward Proposal Gone Wrong (TV News Roundup)

title: Maude Apatow Directorial Debut ‘Poetic License’ Lands at Sony Pictures Classics After Row K Debacle (EXCLUSIVE)
description: The saga over Maude Apatow’s directorial debut has a happy ending. Her TIFF player “Poetic License” will be released by the venerated Sony Pictures
body:
The saga over Maude Apatow’s directorial debut has a happy ending. Her TIFF player “Poetic License” will be released by the venerated Sony Pictures Classics, following a distribution debacle with original buyer Row K Entertainment.

	Variety reported in March that Row K had become inundated with unpaid bills and a creative exodus after less than a year in business. Apatow’s “Poetic License,” starring her mother Leslie Mann and Cooper Hoffman, saw a release date shuffle before the film’s sales reps at WME Independent took the project back out to market. Now, the studio behind “Call Me By Your Name” will roll out the movie in 2027.
	

	The film garnered overwhelmingly positive reviews on its Toronto premiere last September, and SPC took worldwide rights in the negotiation. It follows former therapist and soon-to-be empty nester Liz (Mann), who relocates to a new town for her husband’s job. Her quiet attempt to settle in takes an unexpected turn when she becomes the point of tension between two inseparable best friends and college seniors, Sam (Hoffman) and Ari (Andrew Barth Feldman). As their fierce competition for her attention threatens to upend their lives, Liz is pulled into a tangle of longing, self-discovery, and the intoxicating thrill of being truly seen – forcing her to confront the life she’s built and the one she still craves.


	“I grew up watching and loving the films released by Sony Pictures Classics. They shaped my understanding of what movies could be. To now be working alongside Michael Barker, Tom Bernard and the entire team is a dream come true,” Apatow said in a statement.
	

	Leadership at SPC said the film “marks the arrival of an exciting new chapter for filmmaker Maude Apatow, whose distinctive creative vision is evident in every frame. Equal parts funny and heartfelt, the film features career-best performances from Leslie Mann, Cooper Hoffman, and Andrew Barth Feldman, whose undeniable charm and chemistry light up the screen. We are thrilled to bring Maude’s directorial debut to theaters next year and give audiences the opportunity to experience the same magic we felt when we first saw the film.”

	Apatow directs from a script by Raffi Donatich. Producers include Judd Apatow, Josh Church, Benjamin Hung, Thalia Daniel, Maude Apatow, Olivia Rosenbloom, and Will Greenfield. Executive producers include Jamal Daniel, Michelle Upton, Renee Witt, Harrison Kreiss and Jay Cassidy.

schema.headline: Maude Apatow Directorial Debut ‘Poetic License’ Lands at Sony Pictures Classics After Row K Debacle (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Martin Scorsese and Susan Sarandon Squash Their Children’s Internet Beef in New Jack Henry Robbins Sketch (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Susan Sarandon and Martin Scorsese try and fail to squash the beef between their children in the latest social media sketch from Jack Henry Robbins
body:
Susan Sarandon and Martin Scorsese try and fail to squash the beef between their children in the latest social media sketch from Jack Henry Robbins and Francesca Scorsese, Variety can exclusively reveal.

	The last major development in the “nepo-verse” short series saw Francesca blow up Robbins’ car, an escalation that forced Martin and Sarandon to step in as formal adjudicators. Of course, the meeting between them all doesn’t go as planned, and the wrath of Francesca and the parents’ indifference leads only to more pain for Robbins.
	

	In one moment, Francesca reveals a taser, which she quickly turns on Robbins. He then whines to Martin, “She’s got a taser!” The “Taxi Driver” director is too busy with a stack of papers to look up, but tells his daughter, “Francesca, honey, remember: Taser pretty, but taser ouchie.”


	During an earlier beat, Sarandon asks Francesca, “Can you say something nice about Jack? Ok, I know it’s a little tricky, but just look at him. Maybe you’ll get a clue. Dig deep, use your imagination.” Francesca, after thinking for a moment, then tells Robbins, “You’re tall. Like a monster.” Martin, excited by the progress, says, “Good! Great, cause people love monsters. They love them. They always identify with the monster; they empathize with the monster. That’s fantastic.”

	Robbins told Variety that this collaboration came about after Francesca showed her dad one of his sketches. The Oscar winner was immediately down for a guest role, and Robbins wasted no time writing him into one of his sketches.

	“[Martin] is such a talented actor, it’s crazy. Some of my favorite moments, he improvs,” Robbins said. “I tried my best not to embarrass myself, so I definitely tried to speak as little as humanly possible, but he’s absolutely phenomenal. I couldn’t believe that he wanted to be in my video.”
	

	Robbins also had some praise for his mother, adding, “She’s so underratedly funny, and she was so sharp. That line about my eyebrows was completely improvised. Just watching, they’re such a cute duo, and I thought that my mom was so ready and on it. It was great.”

schema.headline: Martin Scorsese and Susan Sarandon Squash Their Children’s Internet Beef in New Jack Henry Robbins Sketch (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Brittany Snow Joins Sydney Sweeney in ‘The Housemaid’s Secret’
description: Brittany Snow will star in “The Housemaid’s Secret,” joining the previously announced cast of Sydney Sweeney, Kirsten Dunst and Paul Anthony Kelly.
body:
Brittany Snow will star in “The Housemaid’s Secret,” joining the previously announced cast of Sydney Sweeney, Kirsten Dunst and Paul Anthony Kelly. 

	“The Housemaid’s Secret” is the follow-up to 2025’s box office sleeper hit “The Housemaid.” Based on Freida McFadden’s bestselling novel, the sequel picks up as Sweeney’s Millie, who works as a live-in maid for wealthy families, takes a new job — this time keeping house for a woman she’s never allowed to see. Like the initial story, Millie’s employers (Dunst and Kelly portray the spouses) are harboring a dark, sinister secret. Snow will play the character Marybeth, an unassuming receptionist at the husband’s company.
	

	Production on the psychological thriller is expected to start later this year. Paul Feige is returning to direct “The Housemaid’s Secret,” having steered “The Housemaid” to $400 million globally against a $35 million budget. Rebecca Sonnenshine, who adapted the first book, is returning to write the sequel. Lionsgate has slated the movie to open on Dec. 17, 2027.


	Lionsgate intends to turn “The Housemaid” into a major film franchise. Although nothing else has been announced, McFadden has a third novel, “The Housemaid Is Watching,” that’s bound to eventually grace the big screen.

	Snow was recently in Netflix’s breakout series “The Hunting Wives,” which was produced by Lionsgate Television and was renewed for a second season. She’s best known for movies like “John Tucker Must Die,” “Hairspray,” the “Pitch Perfect” trilogy and A24’s “X.”  She is represented by Gersh, Principal Entertainment LA, imPRint, and Sloane, Offer, Weber & Dern.

schema.headline: Brittany Snow Joins Sydney Sweeney in ‘The Housemaid’s Secret’

title: Hollywood’s New Leaders: Class of 2026
description: Leadership can mean leveraging one success to create the next — and navigating hundreds of crucial steps in between. It can also mean being the best
body:
Leadership can mean leveraging one success to create the next — and navigating hundreds of crucial steps in between. It can also mean being the best team player you can be, finding the right story, signing the right client, packaging the right product or developing the right promotional campaign. Variety’s annual New Leaders list celebrates the individuals who provide the connective tissue between idea and execution, messenger and message, property and platform. The honorees — all 40 or under — selected in 2026 represent advancement, innovation, achievement and excellence across a broad spectrum of disciplines, from social media and legal strategy to production, personnel management, artist development and strategic partnerships.

			
			
	Cara Alpert
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				

	Agent, UTA

	Alpert signed Meg Stalter when she was a rising comedy star on the internet — landing a career-changing role on “Hacks” and a starring role in Broadway’s “Oh, Mary!” She has also identified breakout talent like Kareem Rahma, while guiding the careers of Fortune Feimster, Leanne Morgan, Connor Hines and Gabby Windey. She signed Veronika Slowikowska, who recently had a breakout season on “Saturday Night Live,” after discovering her on Instagram; and works as Curry Barker’s talent agent helping secure his role in “Anything but Ghosts.”App I can’t live without: “Uber. I’m an objectively terrible driver, and I’ve made peace with that.”

		
			
			
	Andrea Alvarado
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy Image				
					
				
	Director, comedy series, NetflixAlvarado got her start as a production assistant on “The Next Iron Chef,” but at Netflix, she has worked on shows like 13-time Emmy-nominated “Grace and Frankie” and “Emily in Paris,” the latest season of which debuted at No. 2 on the streamer’s Top 10. She will continue her collaboration with “Emily in Paris” creator Darren Star on his forthcoming comedy series “Uncorked,” which landed at Netflix with a script-to-series commitment last year. What’s her biggest hurdle? “Constant yearning to find a balance of work and personal life. Wanting to give each creator and show attention in addition to chasing my two little boys around.”What piece of advice would you give to your younger self? “It’s OK to binge watch TV … it might become your job one day,” she says.
		
			
			
	Maggie Burkhead
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	Senior VP of programming, Fifth SeasonAs the senior-most woman executive at Fifth Season, the independent film and TV production studio, Burkhead’s slate-juggling has reached Olympic-skill level. Managing more than 60 titles with a knack for compelling water cooler dramas, the programming exec’s wins are considerable this year. “His & Hers,” the Tessa Thompson vehicle, dethroned “The Night Agent” as the most-watched English-language title on Netflix thus far in 2026. On top of another successful season of “Severance,” Burkhead is about to help unleash the anticipated “East of Eden” series adaptation — starring Florence Pugh — for Netflix, already tipped as an awards player, and Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy’s “The Good Daughter” at Peacock.
		
			
			
	Rob Cassandro
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	Talent agent, Innovative Artists EntertainmentClient Isa Briones (“The Pitt”) returns to Broadway in hit musical “Just in Time” while client Maxwell Jenkins takes the wheel of the Mystery Machine as Fred in Netflix’s “Scooby-Doo: Origins.” Other achievements include: “Guiding Carlos Manuel Vesga and Samba Schutte of ‘Pluribus’ during their breakout moment” (Vesga was nominated for an Emmy). For Cassandro, a personal connection is key. “Having a hands-on approach is what I cherish most, and I want to continue growing while maintaining the relationships that are at the heart of what I do,” he says.Worst advice you have ever received? “‘Don’t trust anyone.’ I pride myself on building deep relationships with my colleagues across the industry. We can’t do this alone, and I’m grateful to have a group of people I can trust for advice and support when needed.”
		
			
			
	Madeline Chais
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	VP, series, 20th TelevisionChais works closely with showrunner Meaghan Oppenheimer on “Tell Me Lies” and her new series, “Bastards”; worked with showrunner Elwood Reid on hit broadcast series “Tracker”; and is a driving force behind “Deli Boys,” championing its distinct comedic voice and cultural specificity. Chais points out that she’s proud “of the creative talent I’ve been able to grow inside the 20th Television ecosystem. I was fortunate to get to work with Tyne Rafaeli early in her directing career. Now she’s a fixture at our studio.”What advice would you give to your younger self? “Never apologize for wanting a seat at the table. That mindset starts from the top down, and it’s meant everything to have a leader like Karey Burke, who gives me the space to speak up, build relationships and be a meaningful part of the 20th TV team.”
		
			
			
	Joyce Choi
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	VP, film, Imagine EntertainmentChoi has supported a diverse slate for Imagine including “How to Rob a Bank,” “Whalefall” “The Mosquito Bowl” and “Spaceballs 2.” She’s also spearheading “Dangerously Funny,” about the Smothers brothers’ battle with CBS censors. Choi also landed two highly competitive books, “200 Monas” and “The Last Letter” with Amazon, shepherding both through development into packaging. “Growing up, I wasn’t allowed to watch many movies, so the ones I did manage to see felt especially meaningful. That experience shaped the kinds of stories I gravitate toward today,” she says, noting that “with projects like ‘200 Monas’ and ‘The Last Letter,’ I get to champion movies for the same female audience that first sparked my love for film.”What piece of advice would you give to your younger self? “Keep your eyes on your own paper. Everybody’s on their own journey and timeline, and don’t get so stuck on a past decision you made that you miss the things that are really for you.”
		
			
			
	Mirsada Dassani
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	Senior VP, television development, MiramaxSeries adaptations of beloved “Ella Enchanted” and “Chocolat” with Cynthia Erivo top Dassani’s to-do list for Miramax. “By the time I began my career, I never imagined I’d have the opportunity to develop something I read as a teenager — until last year. I had been tracking ‘The Gallagher Girls’ development for decades and watched as it kept being optioned at various studios for features, but never for television. When the rights became available once again, I chased and courted the author.” Dassani knew Miramax was the underdog in the right fight, “but I — and the rest of our creative package (pilot director and exec producer Brad Silberling) — managed to win the author over.”First job? “My first real industry job was Michael Gordon’s desk at CAA in the international subdivision of the TV lit department. I would definitely say that it formed the bedrock of the rest of my career.”
		
			
			
	Derrick Davis
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	Associate, Del ShawYou wouldn’t be wrong calling Davis an overachiever, and we’d expect it from a legal star rising under the great Nina Shaw. After helping cut the landmark 2024 deal for the James Earl Jones estate to voice an AI version of Darth Vader, Davis contributed to December’s $200 million juggernaut deal between iHeartMedia and top radio personality Charlamagne tha God. He also co-piloted director Gina Prince-Bythewood’s deal to direct Paramount’s tentpole bet “Children of Blood and Bone” and a hat trick of gigs for Laurence Fishburne (“The Amateur,” Netflix’s next season of “The Witcher” and the sci-fi horror “The Astronaut”). He’ll close out the year having advised Rick Famuyiwa on his deal to write and direct Lionsgate’s Dennis Rodman biopic “48 Hours in Vegas” starring LaKeith Stanfield.
		
			
			
	Michael DeVeau
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	Partner, WMEAny talent agency’s future relies on the boldness, taste and fortitude of its homegrown talent. DeVeau is the shining example for WME, starting 13 years ago in the mailroom and rising to partner through the agent trainee program. He works with a wide range of talent at various stages in their careers, closing deals that pivot brands or even lead to Oscar nominations. Lupita Nyong’o, Winston Duke and Aldis Hodge are DeVeau’s banner signings — but he’s elevated stars like Brandon Sklenar (“The Housemaid”) and gotten icons like Angelina Jolie back into the genres where audiences first fell in love with them (her upcoming reunion with action director Doug Liman, “The Initiative”).
		
			
			
	Jason Goldberg
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	Head of global film, Webtoon Prods.Goldberg identifies titles on Webtoon and Wattpad for development into Hollywood hits. Following the success of Tubi’s “Sidelined” series, with the first film premiering at No. 1 in the U.S. and Canada, he produced two films that released concurrently earlier this year: “Kissing Is the Easy Part,” based on a Wattpad webnovel with 32 million reads, premiered Feb. 13 on Tubi, while “Love Me Love Me” hit No. 1 globally on Prime Video, with a sequel announced two weeks later. “It is a miracle to get one film made, but it was really unbelievable having two debut on the exact same date,” he says.What piece of advice would you give to your younger self? “I would tell my 18-year-old self to be OK with admitting you don’t know everything. It’s so important to ask questions and take the time to learn from the people around you. Also, don’t throw away your baggy jeans — you will need them in 2025-2026.”
		
			
			
	Josh Greenberg
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy Image				
					
				
	Counsel, Pryor CashmanGreenberg says he takes “pride in being someone that friends, family and clients trust as their ‘go-to’ person when they need help solving complex problems.” He builds trust with his clients “by being their strategic partner and helping them untangle complicated issues, structure deals and find creative solutions that protect and advance their core business objectives.” That has included advising major gaming companies on acquisitions of user-generated content games, intellectual property and platforms for hosting and distributing video game content, such as Spark Universe’s acquisition of Modrinth and the Essential mod for Minecraft.” He also continues to advise indie producer Kaplan Morrison on corporate and business development matters.What is your next hurdle? “Not allowing ChatGPT-generated contracts and legal advice to drive me absolutely insane,” he says. “AI is not a substitute for a good lawyer, and I’ll keep on repeating that until the day that AI inevitably takes my job.”
		
			
			
	Simone Harris
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	VP, television, Proximity MediaRyan Coogler is done proving himself as a box office king. Now the director and his creative team have TV in their sights, with a vital assist from Harris — who oversees development for Proximity principals Zinzi Coogler, Sev Ohanian and the “Black Panther” helmer. She’s spent a large part of her year prepping the anticipated reboot of “The X Files,” led by Danielle Deadwyler and Himesh Patel. Proximity also recently announced an adaptation of the fantasy YA books “Animorphs”; and Harris serves as co-EP on “Southern Bastards,” a Hulu pilot based on the comic book series about a military vet drawn into a web of crime in a small town.
		
			
			
	Abby Ho
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				

	VP, social media & engagement, Disney Kids & Family“Fan whisperer” is perhaps the coolest job title in this year’s New Leaders class, and it’s a serious undertaking for the Disney exec in charge of social strategy for the company’s kids and family endeavors. Overseeing Disney Jr., Disney Channel and Disney Television Animation, Ho helps originals stay relevant to multiple demographics and keeps conversation high about beloved IP — including “Percy Jackson and the Olympians,” “Phineas and Ferb,” “Sofia the First: Royal Magic” and “Marvel’s Iron Man and his Awesome Friends.” Notably, she helped Miley Cyrus’ “Hannah Montana 20th Anniversary Special” amass 440 million impressions across platforms.

	What is your next hurdle? Why? “There has never been a better or harder time to be a marketer.

	Culture and consumer behavior are fragmenting and shifting faster than ever, but that same speed creates real opportunity for brands to build relevance with younger audiences. Across my career from building fan communities and managing creators at Wattpad, to audience and young adult marketing campaigns at Netflix to social campaigns and franchise storytelling at Disney, I’ve focused on translating audience behavior into marketing systems that turn stories into ongoing cultural engagement and that’s where long-term fandom and growth are actually won or lost.”

	My next hurdle is continuing to navigate that transformation: building ecosystems where content, creators, and platforms work together in real time to grow impact, especially for global franchises trying to keep pace with evolving audience habits. That’s the work I’m most energized by.”

		
			
			
	Jessica Hudson
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	Agent, GershHudson has worked to align talent with the world’s top brands in fashion. She’s negotiated and overseen several campaigns and ambassador relationships, including Chase Infiniti’s global ambassadorship with Louis Vuitton and Jacob Elordi’s global ambassadorship with Cartier. For “Love Story’s” Sarah Pidgeon, she secured a Balenciaga global ambassadorship as well as a partnership with Rhode. What would she tell her younger self? “I’d tell her to have more fun and truly not worry about having it all figured out. She used to get lost in the mission of trying to do things ‘right,’ but there’s a lot of beauty in those potentially imperfect choices she was trying so hard to avoid making,” she says.Greatest recent achievement? “My funny little 10-month-old, who I went into labor with while closing a Super Bowl deal,” she says.
		
			
			
	David Kagan
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	Manager, film, NetflixAction is Kagan’s purview, with recent successes including Artists Equity’s “The Rip.” He’s reteaming with the shingle and Ben Affleck for thriller “Animals,” with Peter Berg’s “The Mosquito Bowl,” the third in the “Extraction” franchise, and “Gears of War” on his docket. He was also instrumental in bringing the Asmodee games “Catan” and “Ticket to Ride” to Netflix. Kagan says “good things come to those who wait” is the worst advice he ever got. “You don’t win anything by waiting on others, and I think moving quickly with the pace of our industry is incredibly important.”What was your first job? “A summer job at a gelato shop on the Upper West Side in New York City — just a couple of blocks from where I grew up.”
		
			
			
	Yeeun Kim
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	Associate, SheppardKim’s clients live on the cutting edge of pop culture. She advised Blackpink’s Lisa on her acting agreement for Netflix Korea’s project “Tygo”; advised Zara on its collaboration with Bad Bunny; and for “Is God Is” playwright Alesha Harris, handled the rights, writer and director agreements for the film adaptation as well as producer agreements with Tessa Thompson’s Viva Maude, Janicza Bravo and Linden Prods. She was advised not to move to the U.S. “I had just begun practicing as a litigation attorney in South Korea, and many believed it would be nearly impossible to rebuild my career in another country,” she says. “However, I chose to see the move not as abandoning my career, but as an opportunity to redefine it — transitioning from litigation to transactional and ultimately building a career in Hollywood.”What piece of advice would you give to your younger self? “Make plans, but hold them loosely,” she says. “Life will not always unfold the way you expect, and learning to adapt can take you somewhere even more rewarding.”
		
			
			
	Aubrey Landon
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy Image				
					
				
	Senior director of creative, Sony Music Publishing NashvilleType Landon’s name and Sony into a search engine together and virtually all of the results are articles and photos about her signing songwriters: Cody Johnson, Randall King, Adam James; her work with hit writers like Brice Long, Jim Beavers (nominated for the Nashville Songwriter Hall of Fame) and Hall of Famer Tom Douglas and artists Drew Baldridge and Gabby Barrett. The Belmont University grad has had just two major jobs since she graduated: Nine years at Young Guns Publishing before she joined Rusty Gaston and the gang at Sony in 2022. It’s not hard to see why: Songwriter Brian Fuller, who signed with Sony in 2024, says, “Aubrey has the drive and work ethic of 10 people and I feel so lucky to have her in my corner.”Greatest recent achievement? “Becoming a mom and now a working mom. Learning that it is possible to have a beautiful family and a thriving career.”
		
			
			
	Meg Lewis
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	VP, production, ParamountLewis was a key part in bringing two of Paramount’s biggest movies of the year to life: “Scream 7” and “Scary Movie.” Lewis spent the past 18 months working on “KPOP: The Debut,” a film releasing Feb. 26 that she calls a “spiritual successor to ‘The Lizzie McGuire Movie.’” Her career in the entertainment industry has taught her many things, but if she could offer one piece of advice to her 18-year-old self, it would be to not think “Pirates of the Caribbean” is an embarrassing answer when asked what her favorite movie is.Forward-thinking philosophy: “Turns out loving movies is a better career strategy than pretending to like the ones you think you’re supposed to,” she says.
		
			
			
	Vivien Mao
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	Producer, the Littlefield CompanyWhile supporting legacy titles such as “The Handmaid’s Tale,” Mao also serves as a co-producer on hit spinoff series “The Testaments,” as well as a co-executive producer on “The Twisted Tale of Amanda Knox.” “Being a part of the development and successful worldwide launch of ‘The Testaments’ was a magical experience. I was an assistant when ‘The Handmaid’s Tale’ was still airing, and to be welcomed into and nurtured by that creative family was really special to me. … It has been incredible to watch this show find its passionate audience. Also, the amount of weekly texts I got from friends and family worldwide (I even had friends in China reaching out!) exuding love for the show was euphoric.” She will also be producing the upcoming Hulu series “Conviction.”Worst advice you have ever received? “‘Wait your turn.’ I think this is often said to slow people down who feel anxious, but who is anyone to tell you when your turn is? Taking active advantage of the opportunities that come your way is a huge part of success.”
		
			
			
	Bentley Moore Patterson
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	VP, exhibitor marketing, Bleecker StreetIn addition to her recent work on “Stray Kids: The dominATE Experience,” Moore Patterson also led the launch of first-party data-sharing partnerships with two of the nation’s largest exhibition circuits, becoming one of Bleecker Street’s most influential strategic initiatives. Moore Patterson is currently working on keeping theatrical moviegoing feeling like an event, inventing new ways to keep audiences going to the cinema. “That’s what makes exhibitor marketing so exciting — every campaign is a new chance to surprise people and remind them why seeing a movie in a theater on the big screen is still a special experience,” she says.
		
			
			
	Claire-Marie Murphy
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	Senior VP, creative and strategy, Universal PicturesAs Disney’s chief rival, Universal Pictures maintains a vast marketing operation to hype its diverse portfolio holdings in tentpoles, prestige dramas, mainstream comedy and kids and family. CMO Michael Moses needs someone like Murphy, his direct report, in a bespoke role that keeps trains running, awareness high and filmmakers happy. The Harvard grad ensures all departments are communicating and the filmmakers are being heard — like Christopher Nolan and Emma Thomas of Syncopy. The Oscar winners had Murphy as their direct creative liaison on all marketing elements for “The Odyssey,” including creative advertising, digital and publicity. Murphy also served on Steven Spielberg’s “Disclosure Day” and will help shepherd new film installments of two crucial franchises: “Focker-in-Law” and “Shrek 5.”
		
			
			
	Eric Perlmutter-Gumbiner
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	Partner, Greenberg GluskerDeft in his work with celebrity-driven consumer brands, Perlmutter-Gumbiner has worked with Kim Kardashian’s Skims in connection with its formation, multiple financings and outside general counsel matters, Khloé Kardashian’s Good American brand and Tom Hanks’ Hanx Coffee. Perlmutter-Gumbiner has advised Barstool Sports on several matters, and is representing Warner Music in connection with multiple M&A and investment transactions. His first job was as a Little League umpire. “It helped develop a strong sense of right and wrong, and a tolerance for dealing with unruly people (the parents),” he says.Greatest recent achievement? “Celebrating my first child’s first birthday,” he says.
		
			
			
	Nick Reynolds
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	VP of film, RidebackRideback, the almost 20-year-old production company established by producer Dan Lin, is certainly looking to new leaders after its founder took the top film job at Netflix in 2024. Reynolds is at the forefront of the post-Lin era, helping develop big IP like the splashy “Sesame Street” feature film package that his team will produce at the streamer. His role is to identify or reawaken valuable titles like “The Partner,” a John Grisham legal thriller adaptation set up at Universal. Jason Bateman will direct Tom Holland in the yarn about a junior lawyer who fakes his own death to help a sketchy client reap millions.
		
			
			
	Matt Sadeghian
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	Manager, Brillstein Entertainment PartnersComedy is serious business to Sadeghian — his clients sell out arenas, theaters and clubs. He also stays on the cutting edge of rising talent. He repped a handful of headliners at the Netflix Is a Joke Festival this year — Morgan Jay, Almost Friday’s Eilise Patton, UpDating, Paul Chowdhry, and Deric Cahill — as well as Jeff Arcuri, whose Netflix Is a Joke shows sold out the Hollywood Palladium almost immediately. Client Trevor Wallace sold out his “Alpha Beta Male” tour earlier this year, adding 38 theaters for a second leg. Sadeghian notes that as an Iranian-American whose father has remained in Iran throughout his life, he is deeply committed to amplifying diverse voices in entertainment. His client Bassem Youssef’s work includes the Scholastic children’s franchise “The Magical Reality of Nadia,” which follows an Egyptian-immigrant protagonist navigating racism and identity; bestselling YA duology “The Similars”; and “The Pretenders” by writer Rebecca Hanover, which tackle themes of otherness through a sci-fi lens.
		
			
			
	Andrew Sanchez
			
										
					Image Credit: Sophie Sahara				
					
				
	CEO, co-founder, UdioSanchez brought Udio to market in 2024 not as a former music industry executive, but as an aspiring academic who dabbled in everything from history to pre-med. Now, he’s the CEO of an AI music generator that’s raised millions, including investment from will.i.am. Next up on Sanchez’s plate, aside from fighting Sony’s most recent lawsuit: getting Udio’s Universal and Warner-backed product to launch. “The major theme here is demonstrating as much as we can how beneficial we think this will be for artists, so that artists participate,” he says. “We want to have a big sort of windfall of artists so that they can see the upside in it.”His first job? “Singing in the choir. I was actually paid to sing in the choir every morning at 8:15 a.m., which was an amazing experience.”
		
			
			
	Charles Scully
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	Manager, the Gotham GroupAmong Scully’s recent highlights are the sale of Dave Matalon’s feature spec “The Worst Man” to Universal with 87 North producing; “With the 8th Pick,” co-written by client Gavin Johannsen and Alex Sohn, sold to Warner Bros. with Star Thrower and Religion of Sports producing; and “Get Lite,” written by Eric Gross, greenlit at Paramount with Teyana Taylor directing. “One thing I didn’t learn in college that would have helped me in the real world was the value of traveling and immersing myself in different cultures. My biggest regret is not studying abroad for a semester and getting out of my university bubble. It’s a lesson I’ve learned from and have made a conscious effort to stay curious and seek out new experiences,” he says.Worst advice you have ever received? “To quit. Whether that was in sports growing up, dropping a class, or even getting into the entertainment industry. Hard work can bring surprising results even in the unlikeliest of outcomes,” he says.
		
			
			
	Pete Spencer
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy Image				
					
				
	VP, development and production, Searchlight PicturesSpencer is prestige label Searchlight Pictures’ man in the U.K., an important territory for indie auteurs (and the increasingly international body of Oscar voters). Overseeing all production in the region, Spencer helped mount Martin McDonagh’s “Wild Horse Nine” — already an Oscar contender and a follow-up to the director’s acclaimed “The Banshees of Inisherin” — as well as Alice Birch’s directorial debut, “Sweetstick,” from star and producer Cate Blanchett. He also manages relationships with key filmmakers including Yorgos Lanthimos and Andrew Haigh.
		
			
			
	Tara Timinsky
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	Books & IP manager, UntitledIn Hollywood, real leadership means results. That more than qualifies Timinsky, who has pushed through significant literary sales and adaptation deals on behalf of clients navigating the dramatic stall in production spends. Over the past year, she’s inked splashy deals for titles like Virginia Evans’ “The Correspondent,” with Jane Fonda attached at Lionsgate; “The Perversion of Justice: The Jeffrey Epstein Story” by Julie K. Brown to Sony; and an adaptation of Annabel Lyon’s “The Golden Mean” for “Heated Rivalry” wunderkind Jacob Tierney and EP Jason Bateman. And those are just the sales we’re allowed to write about.
		
			
			
	Matthew Tinker
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	President, David E. Kelley Prods.Tinker says he has held every job under the sun, from working on an unaired show called “Starfishing,” which took celebrities out to sea, to being a writers’ assistant on shows like “Hawthorne” for TNT. After Tinker’s spec script about young EMTs caught the attention of David E. Kelley, he wound up launching his 14-year (and counting!) career at David E. Kelley Prods., working his way up to president by taking after Kelley’s strong work ethic. The company’s busy slate of upcoming shows includes follow-up seasons to “Big Little Lies,” “Margo’s Got Money Troubles” and “Presumed Innocent.”Quality control: As they expand and look into unscripted and video game adaptations, Tinker stresses that he is always driven by characters first and foremost: “Let the story be the boss of any notes or any processes. Never let the production wag the dog.”
		
			
			
	Mark Tompkins
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy Image				
					
				
	Senior manager, original movies, development & strategy, Amazon MGM StudiosTompkins is passionate about helping shape the studio’s slate “including authoring 20-plus greenlights,” he says — those films include “Highlander,” “Heat 2,” “The Wrecking Crew” and “Voltron.” “One project I’m particularly excited about is ‘Untitled Sham Marriage,’ which I’m overseeing as a development executive. It’s a hilarious rom-com that Stephen Merchant wrote, directed and starred in opposite Cameron Diaz. Point Grey and Lee Eisenberg’s Piece of Work produced the film alongside Stephen,” he says.What is your next hurdle? “Learning to see around corners, champion ideas before they’re obvious and stay humble enough to know I don’t have all the answers. Recognition shouldn’t make me more certain; it should make me more curious. The industry will keep changing, and I want to keep earning the opportunity to help shape where it goes next.”
		
			
			
	Andrew Tsoules
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	Motion picture talent agent, CAATsoules helps oversee an embarrassment of riches at CAA’s storied movie talent group: Adrien Brody, Mahershala Ali, Vanessa Kirby, Andrew Garfield, Carey Mulligan, Jon Bernthal, Channing Tatum and more. He got there by understanding that film stars need consistent reinvention and counterprogramming across their IMDb credits page. Take his closing of Kirby’s deal for “Avengers: Doomsday,” continuing her Marvel run after the harrowing indie “Pieces of a Woman” and the end of Tom Cruise’s “Mission: Impossible” series. He also booked both Garfield and client Jamie Bell on Paul Greengrass’ “The Rising,” and ushered Bernthal into the A-list of “The Odyssey.”
		
			
			
	Cody Verdecias
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner				
					
				
	VP of A&R, Atlantic RecordsCo-founder & president, Deep Love RecordingsTraditionally, record labels reward their top A&R people with labels of their own, and after a string of genre-spanning successes like Grammy-winning rock titans Turnstile, 100 Gecs, Fred Again and others (not to mention his parallel career as manager for Gecs, Dahi, Daytrip, Emile Haynie and more), last year he got his: Deep Love Recordings. The label includes Dallas rockers Empty Shell Casing, regional Mexican duo Corridos Ketamina and DJ Fifi. His wide-ranging rosters are a modern-day reflection of his background: Jane’s Addiction frontman and Lollapalooza founder Perry Farrell is his uncle, and it’s not hard to guess where his love of alternative music flourished (and how he spent every summer as a teen).
		
			
			
	Rebecca Weisberg
			
										
					Image Credit: Chris Schmitt				
					
				
	Senior VP, business affairs, Warner Bros. TelevisionCombining her legal mind and her love of TV, Weisberg handles the business affairs of some of the hottest shows on TV: “The Pitt,” “Georgie & Mandy’s First Marriage,” “Stuart Fails to Save the Universe,” “Untamed” and “Leanne,” and is the lead WBTV business affairs exec on all John Wells Prods. and Chuck Lorre Prods. scripted television development. Her most notable recent achievement? “The dealmaking behind ‘The Pitt.’ We’ve secured the deals necessary to provide long-term stability for both the cast and the creators, giving this extraordinary show the foundation to continue growing and succeeding for years to come.”What piece of advice would you give to your younger self? “If the worst thing anyone can say is ‘no,’ ask every time,” she says. “So many of the biggest opportunities in my life happened because I was willing to ask the question, be direct about what I wanted, send the email and advocate for myself — even when the odds felt impossibly long. Rejection is temporary, but wondering ‘what if?’ lasts a lot longer. So, ask. Take the chance. Go for it.”
		
			
			
	Elizabeth Woodward
			
										
					Image Credit: WILLA				
					
				
	Founder, CEO, WillaWhile Woodward initially set out to focus on production when creating Willa in 2017, the company recently moved into distribution — a move informed by the founder’s strong production experience working on titles like “On the Divide” and shows like “The Vow.” “My guiding lights are being curious and determined,” Woodward says. “Independent film, which is the space that I operate in, requires a lot of passion.” Most recently, Willa picked up Kaouther Ben Hania’s “The Voice of Hind Rajab” after the buzzy Palestinian film struggled to find U.S. distribution. Woodward (an executive producer on the film) saw the opportunity for Willa to step in and have the core filmmaking team be part of every step, leading the film to an Oscar nomination for best international feature. “We took a lot of care to bring the film out into the world in the right way,” she says.What app can’t you live without? “Notes and calculator”

title: Mexican Cartel Boss Arrested For Allegedly Ordering Influencer's Livestreamed Murder
description:
Mexican Cartel Boss
                          Busted For Allegedly Ordering Hit On Beauty Influen
body:
Mexican Cartel Boss
                          Busted For Allegedly Ordering Hit On Beauty Influencer, Mayor
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 4, 2026
                            6:31 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  August 4, 2026
                                10:14 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The leader of a Mexican criminal cartel was swept up by authorities after allegedly ordering the brutal murders of his son's beauty influencer ex-girlfriend and a mayor.
      
    
            Ramón Ángel Álvarez Ayala was arrested in late July by military personnel and law enforcement officers during a joint operation ... according to multiple reports.
      
    
            Mexican officials say Ayala was known as "El R-1" ... he was the main leader of "Los Rs", one of the most violent criminal organizations connected to the Jalisco New Generation Cartel -- a group allegedly involved in murder, extortion and drug trafficking. 
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            According to authorities, Ayala masterminded and financed the hit on 23-year-old beauty influencer Valeria Marquez -- whose ex-boyfriend is Ayala's son. In May 2025, Marquez was shot and killed by a gunman while livestreaming in her beauty salon in the Mexican city of Zapopan.
      

            The gunman was seen on video pretending to be a delivery driver. He asked to confirm her name, and then shot her in the head and chest, causing her to collapse while the livestream was still up and running.  
      
    
            Omar Hamid García Harfuch, Mexico's Secretary of Security and Citizen Protection, said Marquez's murder was connected to Ayala's son, Francisco Álvarez, who allegedly threatened Márquez after they broke up.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Authorities have arrested another man in connection with Márquez's murder, but it's unclear if he's the gunman.
      
    
            Police are still searching for Francisco. 
      
    
            In addition, Harfuch said Ayala financed and ordered the execution of Carlos Alberto Manzo Rodríguez, the mayor of Uruapan, a city in the Mexican state of Michoacán.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Manzo -- who often spoke out against organized crime -- was shot to death during the "Day of the Dead" celebrations in November 2025.
      
    
            Harfuch said 31 people have been arrested in connection with Manzo's killing.

title: Tom Sandoval Alleges Ex-GF Victoria Kicked Him, Yelled 'You Have a Tiny Penis' During Attack
description:
Tom Sandoval on Ex-GF Victoria
                          My Ex Berated Me About 'Tiny Penis'
body:
Tom Sandoval on Ex-GF Victoria
                          My Ex Berated Me About 'Tiny Penis'
                          During Alleged Attack
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 4, 2026
                            8:00 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  August 4, 2026
                                10:18 AM PDT
                                    
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Tom Sandoval claims his ex, Victoria Lee Robinson, kicked him in the groin and questioned his manhood during a nasty altercation when they were still dating ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            The "Vanderpump Rules" alum submitted a new declaration Monday in his ongoing restraining order case against his ex, claiming the alleged groin-kick happened in October while he was on tour with his band "Tom Sandoval and the MOST Extras" in Florida.
      
    
            Tom says after the concert ended, Victoria "kicked me repeatedly in the groin area while hurling expletives and insults toward me in the presence of my band mates, tour crew and fans."
      
    
            He claims Victoria had "consumed drugs and alcohol to the point that venue security personnel had to physically carry her from the concert venue back to the tour bus" earlier in the night.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Victoria allegedly attacked Tom when he returned to his tour bus to check on her. He claimed, "she kicked my groin area with her legs and yelled insults such as 'You have a tiny f****** penis! F*** you!'"
      
    
            Tom also says multiple venues expressed concern about Victoria's alleged drug use backstage and claims she invited fans backstage and shared drugs with them. He says her behavior was so concerning, his band manager and musical director "expressed that they wanted to ban her from continuing on the tour."
      
    
            In the court filing, Tom also alleges Victoria created drama that caused him repeated "distress and anxiety," saying her antics left him "frazzled" and "anxious" before his "America’s Got Talent" performance at the show's August 2025 quarterfinals.
      
    
      
        
              
    
    
            He claims Victoria continuously made comments like he's "not a real man" that diminished his self-confidence ... but he says he stayed with her because "she threatened to ruin my life if I left her."
      
    
            Tom also claims, "[Victoria] repeatedly told me and others that she would destroy my life and 'get the Ariana [Madix] treatment,' referring to the public attention and career opportunities my former girlfriend received after our breakup."
      
    
            Victoria tells TMZ ... "I did not kick Tom, and I did not touch him. I had taken a shot and asked him to take care of me; he chose not to."
      
    
            She added, "I went back to bed on the bus and asked him to keep the noise down. That's what actually happened. I am trying to move on with my life, and I keep getting pulled back into this."
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported, Tom was granted a temporary domestic violence restraining order against Victoria and her father, Will Robinson, at the end of June.
      
    
            Victoria tried to obtain a temporary protective order of her own against Tom, but it was denied until a future hearing.
